findings.title: The derived 30-day ceiling omits unheld provider spend and double-counts re-submits
findings.description: `ceiling_values` (scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:88-91), `ceiling_command` (94-97) and the cap check in `judge_estimate` (line 244, `planned + trailing > cap_30d`) all work from `planned + trailing`. The guard that will actually authorise the purchase computes the breach differently: `evaluate_spend` in src/manta_trading/data/tick/spend_guard.py sums `trailing_total + unheld_total + planned_new`, where `unheld_total` is the cost of provider jobs no manifest row holds (the estimate itself reports these as `unheld_jobs`) and `planned_new` deliberately excludes re-submits whose cost is already inside `trailing`. Two consequences: (a) the command the PM is told to run can set a `--cap-30d` below what the guard demands, so the purchase it enables is still refused by `mt data tick pass`; (b) the cutover's own check is looser than the guard when unheld jobs exist and stricter than the guard for a re-submit (that cost is counted once in `planned` and again in `trailing`, while the guard counts it once). No test covers unheld jobs in the ceiling derivation (`test_ceiling_command_rounds_the_estimate_up_to_the_next_five` and `test_an_over_ceiling_estimate_carries_the_command_for_its_figures` only use `planned`/`trailing`).

findings.title: The --estimate run never narrates the estimate's refusal reasons
findings.description: `_estimate_only` prints `verdict {summary['verdict']}: {outcome}` (line 271) and then, whenever the outcome is `BUY`, the ceiling command (line 274) — but it never narrates `summary["reasons"]`, the list the planner fills with why the estimate was refused (absent or short ceilings, archive space short, provider costs). The full path does surface them: `judge_estimate` raises with `summary["reasons"]` (scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:249-252), so the estimate path loses exactly the information the operator needs to choose the ceilings. The output is also self-contradictory: with `check_ceilings=False`, `judge_estimate` returns `BUY` for every verdict other than `nothing_to_buy` (scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:232-233), so a plan refused for a non-ceiling reason still yields "verdict refused: buy", a ceiling command and exit code 0. No test asserts on the estimate's reasons.

findings.title: EXIT_USAGE is dead code
findings.description: `EXIT_USAGE = 2` was added but never referenced: the usage exit code comes from argparse's own `SystemExit`, which `main` converts with `return int(exc.code or 0)` (line 236). Either use the constant there or drop it, so the exit-code vocabulary has one home.

findings.title: A failed gate-issue lookup loses gh's stderr
findings.description: `check_gate_issue` wraps `view(number)` and reports `f"gate issue #{number}: gh failed: {exc}"`. `out()`/`run()` capture stderr but `CalledProcessError.__str__` carries only the command and the exit status, so the operator sees "gh failed: Command '['gh', 'issue', 'view', '69', ...]' returned non-zero exit status 1" with no reason (not authenticated, wrong repository, issue not found). Passing the captured stderr into the message would keep the stop explainable.

findings.title: Over-session names are not attributed to the family they belong to
findings.description: The statistics coverage document's `volume_checks` carry one verdict per volume family (tick tier and `bar_1m` — see `tick_coverage_statistics._volume_checks`), and each rendered verdict has a `family` key. `over_sessions` (line 105) drops that key, and `_family_evidence` accumulates the names per product only, so `over_failures` (line 119) prints the same product-wide list under every family row that has an `over` count. A session from the tick tier can therefore be named under the `ohlcv-1m` failure line. Keeping the family in the extracted name (or keying `named` by product and family) would keep the D6 report pointing at the right family.

structured_findings.summary: The derived 30-day ceiling omits unheld provider spend and double-counts re-submits
The --estimate run never narrates the estimate's refusal reasons
A failed gate-issue lookup loses gh's stderr
Over-session names are not attributed to the family they belong to
